leftColumn.title: Bilateral Forwards (Pre-1848)
leftColumn.subtitle: Custom & High Default Risk
bullets: Private agreements between farmer and merchant
Zero collateral; 100% dependent on counterparty honor
Complete default when spot market dropped 50%
Illiquid with massive bid-ask search costs

rightColumn.title: Standardized Futures (CBOT 1848+)
rightColumn.subtitle: Clearinghouse Novation
bullets: Standardized contract quantities and delivery dates
Clearinghouse acts as buyer to seller and seller to buyer
Daily mark-to-market variation margins guarantee solvency
Zero counterparty default risk in 175+ years of operation

cards.title: 1. The 10-Year Fixed Liability
cards.desc: MGRM guaranteed fixed-price oil delivery to customers over 10 years totaling 160 million barrels.

cards.title: 2. The Short-Dated Stack-and-Roll
cards.desc: Because 10-year futures did not exist, MGRM bought short-term 1-month futures and rolled them monthly.

cards.title: 3. The Contango Roll Trap
cards.desc: Oil plunged and flipped into contango; MGRM had to buy high and sell low every single monthly roll.

cards.title: 4. The $1.3B Cash Margin Drain
cards.desc: Daily variation margins drained cash reserves completely, forcing early liquidation at massive losses.

beats.en_narration: Futures force full locked payment even when prices crash; options cap maximum loss at upfront premium.

beats.en_subtitle: Futures force locked payment if prices crash; options cap loss at premium.

leftColumn.title: Linear Futures Obligation
leftColumn.subtitle: Symmetric Commitment
bullets: Strict obligation to take delivery at locked forward price
If spot market collapses, you must still pay the high locked price
Daily variation margin demands create extreme cash stress
Zero participation in favorable downward spot rallies

rightColumn.title: Asymmetric Option Convexity
rightColumn.subtitle: Contingent Protection
bullets: Right, but never obligation, to exercise at strike price K
Maximum possible downside loss strictly capped at upfront premium
Retains 100% participation in favorable market price swings
No daily variation margin calls for long option holders

subtitlePhrases.text: Futures force locked payment if prices crash;

cards.title: 1. The Pre-1973 Deadlock: Drift (mu)
cards.desc: Economists believed option value depended on subjective investor optimism regarding expected stock drift (mu).

cards.title: 2. The Delta-Replication Portfolio
cards.desc: Construct a self-financing portfolio: Long 1 Call Option, Short Delta shares of underlying stock.

cards.title: 3. Drift mu Vanishes Completely
cards.desc: Because delta continuously removes directional price risk, the portfolio is risk-free and must earn rate r.

cards.title: 4. Risk-Neutral Valuation Law
cards.desc: All derivatives can be evaluated under risk-neutral probability without guessing future market trends.

leftColumn.title: Pre-1987 Black-Scholes Theory
leftColumn.subtitle: Constant Volatility Myth
bullets: Assumed constant volatility sigma across all strike prices
Log-normal bell curve pricing with infinitesimal tail probabilities
Out-of-the-money puts traded at very cheap flat premiums
Completely blind to sudden 20%+ single-day systemic crashes

rightColumn.title: Post-1987 Volatility Smile
rightColumn.subtitle: Crashophobia & Fat Tails
bullets: Deep out-of-the-money puts command massive implied volatility premiums
Markets explicitly price fat left tails and jump-to-default risk
Implied volatility surface curves upward across strike and maturity
Empirical proof that real financial markets demand crash insurance

messages.text: Sharma ji, now I finally see the whole picture! No chapter stands alone—futures provide low-cost locks, options cap tail risk, and Greeks engineer the hedge.
Exactly! Measure basis with futures, cap ruin with options, dynamically rebalance with the Greeks, and price extreme crash risk with the volatility smile.

ui_state.heading: THE 8 INVIOLABLE LAWS OF DERIVATIVES
steps: 1. Exchange novation eliminates bilateral counterparty credit risk.
2. Forward price is locked by cash-and-carry financing arbitrage: F0 = S0 * exp((r-q)T).
3. Linear futures forfeit upside and demand continuous cash variation margins.
4. Convex options grant asymmetric upside while strictly capping downside loss.
5. Dynamic delta hedging eliminates subjective asset drift mu from option valuation.
6. Single-Greek hedging creates catastrophic gamma and vega vulnerability.
7. Flat volatility is an illusion; post-1987 crashophobia creates volatility smiles.
8. No derivative stands alone; true risk engineering unites all tools into one fortress.
